title: The universal form (11.9–11.31)
hook: Arjuna gets what he asked for, and it's brighter than a thousand suns

segments.voice: Yesterday: divyam chakshuh — Arjuna asks to see, and gets a divine eye. Your line was show me. Today, he's shown. Day one hundred ninety-seven.

One sun at noon is already too bright to look at. Add a second beside it. Then ten. Then a hundred. Then a thousand, all at once, all blazing. You can't look at it. You can't look away. That's the measure the Gita reaches for at the moment Arjuna, with his new divine eye, finally sees what he asked to see. Sanjaya, telling it, has no ordinary comparison left, so he stacks up suns. Today, the vision itself.
screen: `ONE SUN AT NOON.` → `THEN A THOUSAND, AT ONCE.` → `TOO BRIGHT TO LOOK AT.`

segments.voice: Sanjaya, the narrator, tells it. Having spoken, the great lord of yoga showed Arjuna his supreme form. Many mouths and eyes, many wonders, divine ornaments, divine weapons raised. Faces turned in every direction. And verse twelve: if the light of a thousand suns were to blaze up in the sky all at once, it might be like the splendor of that great being. Verse thirteen: there, in the body of the god of gods, Arjuna saw the whole universe, divided in countless ways, gathered as one. His hair stands on end. He bows his head, joins his palms, and starts to speak. At first it's wonder. I see all the gods in your body, and all kinds of beings. Brahma on his lotus, the sages, the divine serpents. I see you everywhere, with countless arms and eyes. No end, no middle, no beginning. The sun and moon are your eyes. And then it turns. The mouths have fangs. The worlds are trembling, and so am I. And Arjuna sees the warriors of both armies, the men he's about to fight, his own teachers and great-uncle among them, rushing into those mouths, like rivers running into the ocean, like moths flying into a flame. Some are caught between the teeth. It's beautiful and it's terrifying, and the Gita doesn't soften either. Verse thirty-one: tell me, who are you, in this fierce form? I bow to you. Be gracious. I want to understand you; I don't know what you're doing. That's the word today, the universal form: everything, seen at once, including the parts that frighten us.
screen: `FACES IN EVERY DIRECTION.` · `THE LIGHT OF A THOUSAND SUNS.` · `NO END, NO MIDDLE, NO BEGINNING.` · `LIKE MOTHS INTO A FLAME.` · then, large: `WHO ARE YOU?`

segments.voice: Sit, and start small: feel your own body, breathing. Then widen. Picture the room, the building, the street. Keep widening: the city, the whole country at this hour, people waking and sleeping, being born and dying. Then the earth, turning in sunlight. Let it be too big to hold. Notice what that feels like: wonder, fear, both. Then come back to one breath. The bell holds the time.
Vishvarupa. The universal form: the whole universe seen at once in God's body, brighter than a thousand suns, wonderful and terrible.
Your line: a thousand suns. Step outside once today, look near the sun without looking at it, and imagine a thousand. Day one hundred ninety-seven.

howItsDone: The vishvarupa, the universal form of Gita chapter eleven, is painted, sculpted and staged across Hindu art and temple traditions, and many devotees read the chapter with awe as the Gita's great vision.

match.prompt: what's inside the vision — tap the pairs.
pairs: the light of a thousand suns

myth: the vision is only beautiful and calm
it turns terrifying: fangs, trembling worlds, warriors rushing into the mouths.
in the vision, the warriors rush into the mouths like rivers into the sea
verse 28: like rivers running to the ocean; verse 29: like moths into a flame.
Arjuna understands the vision right away
verse 31: who are you, in this fierce form? I don't know what you're doing.

fork.setup: you're Arjuna. you asked to see God's true form, and it's more terrible than you imagined. what do you do?
options: close your eyes and refuse to look.
bow, and ask: who are you, in this fierce form?
fork.reveal: he bows and asks, verse 31: tell me who you are. be gracious. the answer comes tomorrow.

original.note: Sanskrit: vishvarupa, the universal form; vishva (all, the universe) + rupa (form).

trapdoor: what you thought: seeing God would be peaceful.
what it means: the universal form shows everything at once, creation and destruction, brighter than a thousand suns, and it overwhelms Arjuna.
what a scholar hears: 11.12's 'divi surya-sahasrasya' gave Robert Jungk's 1956 book its title; the chapter is called vishvarupa-darshana yoga, the yoga of seeing the universal form.

sources.ref: Bhagavad Gita 11.9–11.14 (the form revealed; a thousand suns)
Bhagavad Gita 11.15–11.31 (Arjuna's description; who are you?)
Robert Jungk, Brighter than a Thousand Suns (German 1956, English 1958)

notes: All verses paraphrased; Arnold 1885 (The Song Celestial) has a public-domain rendering of 11.12, but it isn't quoted because its exact wording couldn't be confirmed.
Jungk's book: German 'Heller als tausend Sonnen' (1956), English 1958. The voice says 'in 1956 a book... took its title'; confirm.
Check the vision's details: Brahma on the lotus (11.15), no end/middle/beginning (11.16), sun and moon as eyes (11.19), rivers into the ocean and moths into flame (11.28–29).
